items.stem: A seller behaves as a 'trusted advisor' primarily when they:

options.text: Always agree with whatever the customer says
options.rationale: Blind agreement is not advice; it adds no value.

options.text: Prioritise the customer's long-term interest, even when it slows a deal
options.rationale: Correct: putting the customer's interest first is what builds trust.

options.text: Hide information that might delay a sale
Push the highest-margin product regardless of fit
options.rationale: Self-serving recommendations undermine the advisor role.

items.explanation: Correct: putting the customer's interest first is what builds trust.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A stakeholder power map in an enterprise account is used to:

options.text: Rank stakeholders only by job title
options.rationale: Title alone does not capture influence or interest.

options.text: Understand who influences the decision and how they view the solution
options.rationale: Correct: a power map captures influence and stance to guide engagement.
Pricing is separate from mapping stakeholders.

options.text: Replace the need to talk to stakeholders
options.rationale: A map guides, but does not replace, real engagement.

items.explanation: Correct: a power map captures influence and stance to guide engagement.

items.stem: Which TWO belong in a useful enterprise account plan? (Select TWO)

options.text: Specific account objectives tied to the customer's goals
options.rationale: Correct: objectives linked to customer goals keep the plan relevant.
Correct: whitespace shows where value can grow in the account.

options.text: A promise to avoid ever discussing risks
options.rationale: Ignoring risks weakens, not strengthens, a plan.

options.text: A single contact who owns the whole relationship alone
options.rationale: Relying on one contact is a risk, not a plan strength.
